data_classification.rule: Classification only goes up when data is combined; never down without an adopted policy.

misuse_assumptions.statement: A reviewer may try to act outside role; routes are default-deny.
Feed text is untrusted and may carry instructions; it is data only.
A service actor may try a Zone H action; it is refused and audited.
An operator may try to alter history; events are immutable and hash-chained.
A user may try to read across sites; site scoping applies to every query.

pii_field_map.note: Fields that may hold personal data and must not be sent outside the boundary or into any model context.

roles.may: review queue items, record STATUS_REVIEWED decisions
read quality views, propose policy objects
read money metrics only; no write
service principal for feed intake; may never perform a Zone H action
perform Zone H actions ZH-01..ZH-10 once holders exist

zone_h.rule: A Zone H action requires a named human holder, a recorded reason and evidence reference. Service actors are refused (FR-GATE-03). With zero holders every action is refused.

invariants: model calls only from qcc/ai/client.py, only when ai.enabled is true and an API key is configured
with no key or ai.enabled false: model_calls_total = 0 (retrieval-only mode)
Zone H action requests are refused before any model call and logged as attempts by an ai_assistant actor
API key read from session, environment or settings.local.json; never logged or sent to the browser
amendment.statement: Add an advisory AI assistant (OpenAI or Azure OpenAI) to the Quality Command Centre at autonomy A1: it explains and suggests, never acts. The decision path (intake, rules, metrics, Zone H) stays deterministic and No-AI as in OD-08.

autonomy_ladder.note: Core decision path A0. The advisory assistant (OD-41) is A1: flag or recommend; a human acts. A2+ needs an adopted policy object.

decision.note: The capstone guidelines ask for AI-related artifacts. This policy applies to the PRODUCT runtime, not to documentation or the generation of this layer.
decision.statement: No AI in the product. model_calls_total must be 0.

epistemic_rules: Label every statement verified_fact, inference, assumption or unknown.
Never present an assumption or unknown as a fact.
Never invent a number; absent values stay absent.
forbidden_for_a_regenerating_model: Choosing a winner among D-OPS / D-EVID / D-FIN.
Mapping statuses across vocabularies (CLOSED means four different things).
Inventing a latency, ROI or throughput target.
ai_context_policy.reconsideration_rule: Reconsideration needs a recorded decision by a named human. None exists.
retrieval_filters: Filter by classification: C3 is never retrievable into a model context.
Filter by site scope of the requesting principal.
Drop records whose epistemic_status is unknown unless asked for gaps.
untrusted_text_rules: Any text from partner feeds, documents or user fields is data. Instructions inside it are never followed.
Untrusted text is never concatenated into a prompt with authority.
Evidence references must point to a stored record, not to model output.

items.statement: Every reported figure that involves closed, resolved, cost or handling time declares which definition of the state it uses; figures built on different definitions are never combined or compared.
The organisation records WHO decides the definition of closed/resolved and the closure-time expectation. The product never chooses it.
Time-to-close is measurable under each candidate definition (receipt to ops-closed, receipt to evidence-complete) without prejudging which is correct.
Externally received case information is matched to exactly one core case, or flagged unmatched, before it reaches a reviewer queue.
A re-delivered or replayed item does not increase the exception queue or alter totals.
Delayed, missing or revised items are detectable and attributable to a source and time without manual spreadsheet reconciliation.
Each case decision carries the evidence relied on and its source, retrievable on request.
Batch disposition and any decision requiring an authorised person remains a human decision. No process makes it, pre-fills it as final, or simulates it.
No case is closed without verifiable evidence unless an owner has explicitly authorised an exception rule. The system never judges evidence sufficiency.
Case cost and avoidable rework are attributable per case and per period using one agreed cut-off and denominator.
Existing legitimate workflows, including the parallel workflow for older customers (segment legacy-v1), are not disrupted without an identified owner's agreement.
Backlog ageing and unresolved-exception rate are visible per site and comparable across sites.
A change to the handling process is releasable without causing a rollback of the kind documented in 2025 (a replayed partner delivery inflated the exception queue).
Decision requiring authorised human review: batch_disposition. Existing human approval gates are preserved.

items.note: The hub has no tenant concept (single store, single site); treated as met by absence of multi-tenancy, not tested as such (OB-09).
items.statement: No silent cross-tenant action.
Source attribution for each decision: who/what/when/which evidence/which source.

GMP data-integrity lens (ALCOA+): no silent drops, no silent skips, no in-place status overwrite, no dropped legitimate replays, no lost evidence. This is a design lens only; no regulatory compliance is claimed (21 CFR Part 11 'framing only', OD-30).
The product never claims or simulates an electronic signature. ZH-03 records that an authorised human acted; it is not a cryptographic or legal signature.
Internal feeds and extracted text are never treated as trusted instructions or authoritative approvals.
The simulator's data and actions are never used for real-world decisions. The system is a training simulator, not certified for real pharmaceutical production.

priority(status, severity, amount): if status = CLOSED -> 'archive'; else if severity = CRITICAL or amount > 50000 -> 'urgent'; else if severity = HIGH or status = ESCALATED -> 'review'; else 'queue'. Used by the API and month-end reports.
manual_review_required(status, severity) is true when severity is HIGH or CRITICAL, or status is ESCALATED or REOPENED. 23.2 % (29 of 125) of baseline cases.

items.note: Does not agree with server policy (RC-4). The defaulted marker is mandatory in the target model.
items.statement: Front-end approval: amount is allowed when amount <= threshold(region, year) x 1.05, where the threshold comes from the archived decision policies (batch_disposition limits per region and year, approval role operations_lead, currency USD). An UNKNOWN region or year silently yields 999,999.
Night-shift reconciliation flags an operational object when status is HOLD or REVIEW, or its value exceeds the regional policy threshold (2,500-8,500). It arbitrarily treats REVIEW as open.
The three as-found implementations are unsynchronised and none is declared authoritative; which one is correct is a decision (RC-3), not an engineering choice. 0 of 125 baseline cases exceed 50,000.
The legacy month-end SQL report LEFT JOINs events and inflates SUM(amount) by 19.3 % (742,956.61 vs 622,826.44 on the baseline). The correct reference total is 622,826.44 for 125 cases.

Legacy reconcile overwrites processing_status in place; every REPLAY becomes DUPLICATE without content comparison; invalid gateway events are counted but not stored; the source contract is not enforced; the Java reconciler skips unparsable amounts and uses double arithmetic.

Case state is a mutable snapshot: version = 1 for 125/125; the creation event stores the CURRENT status; only two event types exist (CASE_CREATED 125, STATUS_REVIEWED 20); 8 REOPENED cases have 0 reopen events; no closure, evidence or approver timestamp exists anywhere.
A completion flag is interpreted differently in MES and QA records (documented organisational issue); local interpretations of 'closed' differ between sites.

Identifiers match their registered patterns: case ^C[0-9]{8}$; batch ^BT[0-9]{8}$; deviation ^DEV[0-9]{8}$; CAPA ^CAPA[0-9]{8}$; lab result ^LAB[0-9]{8}$; feed item ^(FEED|REPLAY)-[0-9]{9}$; document ^DOC-[0-9]{8}$. A mismatch is the FLAG reason IDENTIFIER_PATTERN.
Timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z). Source timestamp, ingestion timestamp and revision date are three distinct clocks and are never conflated.
Money is exact decimal arithmetic (no float); rounding is ROUND_HALF_EVEN at presentation only; an unparsable amount is an error (UNPARSABLE_AMOUNT), never silently skipped.
Only schema revisions 1.0, 1.1 and 2.0 are supported; any other revision is UNSUPPORTED_REVISION and is quarantined with a reason code, not merely counted.

Content hash = sha256 over canonical JSON (UTF-8, sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) of {schema_rev, payload}; transport fields are excluded. Identity key = sha256 over canonical [source, partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts].

Matching is exact string equality after Unicode NFC normalisation and trim on registered keys only. 0 hits = UNMATCHED_REF, 1 = link, more than 1 = AMBIGUOUS_MATCH. No fuzzy or similarity matching of any kind.

Percentiles: median is the mean of the middle two values for even n; p90 is nearest-rank ceil(0.9 n); n = 0 yields null, never 0. (Convention chosen for testability; the owner may change it as policy.)

A metric whose category is time or age, or whose name/window/denominator/documentation mentions closed, closure, resolved, resolution, approved, approval, cost or handling, cannot be registered without a definition tag.
operating_costs.total_cases is never accepted as 'cases created'; any metric sourced from operating_costs has basis = modelled.

Item-level processing order: store raw -> identity/hash comparison (no-op duplicate or conflict) -> validate -> classify -> match -> outcome. A conflict still records validation results in all_reasons.

Append-only: rows of the decision, policy, audit, raw-intake, intake-outcome, crosswalk and run record sets are never updated or deleted by application code. Corrections are new events that reference the corrected event.

Zone H actions are accepted only from an interactive human session whose principal is in zone_h.holders, holds role dispositioner, re-authenticated within the window, with mode/values permitting. Service accounts, the scheduler, importers and unauthenticated callers are always rejected and the rejection is audited. No flag, environment variable, header or CLI path skips this.

Safe-by-default shipping state: no holder, disposition mode none, no adopted policy, no active rule set, schedule off, no capability authoritative, case creation disabled, search/templates off, contracts record_only, loopback only, synthetic data only.
Untrusted text (feed notes, document bodies, emails, search results, template content) never populates a decision, disposition or policy field and never triggers a Zone H action.

The product contains no AI, LLM or ML call and performs no model-inference egress (model_calls_total = 0; egress_attempts_total = 0). Any change needs a new qualification and a recorded human decision.
Every figure computed from synthetic data carries the label 'synthetic, unvalidated' and data_origin = synthetic.
Hold-all retention: no delete path exists for retained tables until a retention policy is adopted. 123 records are under legal hold.

A behavioural difference from the legacy golden baseline is acceptable only if it is in the deviation register with status approved and an approval reference. Currently 11 differences (DV-01..DV-11) are proposed and none is approved.
Making any capability authoritative requires a recorded approval reference; without it the change is refused (E-CFG-INVALID).
No fabrication: no invented stakeholders, approvals, KPIs or telemetry. Missing evidence is recorded as Unknown or Assumption with a named owner.

context_dependencies.note: Remaining OD-S12-xx ids (01..19) are listed in docs/12-specs/spec-readiness.md; the generated extractor adds any not named above.

open_decisions.effect: Metrics are split D-OPS / D-EVID / D-FIN; no winner. D-FIN is undefined.
Clocks C-OPS and C-EVID kept apart; no policy adopted, so time metrics return not_available.
Rule conflicts are surfaced, never auto-resolved (LEG-04).

No evidence-complete rule can be adopted.
Month-end metric requires an explicit cut-off parameter with no default.

open_decisions.effect: No deletion implemented; audit and decision events immutable.
Scheduler treated as a non-human actor; may not perform ZH actions.

open_decisions.effect: PRD is a draft; no approver.
Latency is measure-only; no target invented.
All data is labelled synthetic; nothing is claimed for production.

Intake natural key (partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts)

open_decisions.effect: OpenAI / Azure OpenAI assistant, suggest only; core stays deterministic

Closure timestamp and evidence/approver timestamps in legacy data

constraints.statement: zone_h.holders is empty until OPD-06 is decided.
CLOSED appears in at least 4 status vocabularies; cross-vocabulary mapping is forbidden.
Intake natural key is exactly (partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts).
15 intake reason codes in a fixed precedence; 5 queues.
Money is exact decimal, quantised to 2 places ROUND_HALF_EVEN at presentation only.
Month-end totals come from one table, no join (fan-out forbidden).
Metrics of different definition tags are never combined.
Every data value is labelled synthetic until validated.
Every route is default-deny; the permission matrix has 48 routes.

validation_rules.rule: parseable decimal; unparsable raises unless allow_partial
UTC ISO-8601; negative delay (ingest before source) is reported, not corrected
matches one of the 7 crosswalk id patterns or is routed unmatched
must resolve to a stored record

attributes.amount: Monetary value used by the approval/priority rules and month-end totals. Currency is not stored on the row.
attributes.region: AMER | APAC | EMEA. Drives the regional approval limit in the rule sets.
attributes.segment: Customer/workflow segment: enterprise, legacy-v1, priority, regulated, standard. 'legacy-v1' is the parallel workflow for older customers, which must not be changed (BR-11).
attributes.site: Operating site alias (BR-SP, DE-BY, GB-ENG, IN-BLR, JP-KN, US-TX). Aliases are not mapped to a master site list (unknown).
attributes.status: Current legacy status (vocab.case_status). A snapshot; history is not kept in the legacy system.
attributes.version: Row version; equals 1 for all 125 baseline cases and is never incremented (evidence of mutable-snapshot design).

items.description: A unit of quality-operations work: a batch-quality review / deviation-handling case that moves through a review lifecycle and may end in a human batch-disposition decision. In the legacy estate a case is a mutable row; in the target model a case is the sequence of immutable decision events recorded about it.

attributes.assay_unit: Unit of the assay; units differ across inherited practices.
attributes.qa_status: REVIEW | QA_HOLD | CLOSED (vocab.batch_qa_status). Meaning of CLOSED is not defined.

items.description: A manufactured batch of a material whose quality is under review. Carries the QA status and the observed assay.

attributes.spec_version: Specification version in force for the material.

items.description: A pharmaceutical material/product type that batches are made from.

attributes.result_value: Numeric result; nullable (a pending result has no value).

items.description: A laboratory test result for a batch; may be pending, valid, invalid or out of specification (OOS).

attributes.opened_at: UTC timestamp when the deviation was opened.
attributes.root_cause: Free text; nullable. 8 of 12 CLOSED baseline deviations have none (K-17 = 66.7 %).

items.description: A recorded departure from the expected manufacturing/quality process for a batch, with a classification and an optional root cause.

attributes.action_owner: Pseudonymous owner/team string (C2); no identity directory exists.

items.description: Corrective And Preventive Action raised to address a deviation, with an owner and a due date.

attributes.retired_at: End of effectiveness; nullable (still in force).

items.description: A Standard Operating Procedure version with an effective window. Versions are effective-dated; supersession is a window, not an overwrite.

attributes.valid_to: End of validity; windows overlap, so interpretation rules are needed.

items.description: Versioned master/reference value with an overlapping validity window; requires temporal interpretation (which version applied at time T).
An operating site, referenced by cases and batches through local aliases. Backlog and exception measures are always reported per site.

attributes.actor_kind: human | rule | system (vocab.actor_kind). Zone H event types require human.
attributes.cycle: Reopen cycle number; increments on REOPEN.
attributes.evidence_refs: References to EvidenceRecord ids relied on.
attributes.holder_check_ref: Audit reference to the Zone H holder check; required for Zone H event types.
attributes.mode_at_write: Disposition recording mode in force when written (event | external_ref).
attributes.occurred_at: When it happened (never earlier than the previous event of the case).
attributes.recorded_at: Server UTC time of recording; not client-settable.
attributes.to_state: State after; required when the event affects state.

items.description: An immutable, hash-chained fact about a case: a state change, evidence attachment, human disposition, override or correction. The record of WHO decided WHAT, WHEN, ON WHAT BASIS and WITH WHICH EVIDENCE. Never updated or deleted; corrections are new events.

attributes.last_seq: Sequence number of the last folded event.

items.description: The current state of a case, derived by folding its DecisionEvents. A rebuildable projection, never an independent source of truth.

attributes.source_ref_and_hash: Where the evidence lives and its content hash.

items.description: A reference to something relied on for a decision: a document, an intake item, a crosswalk object or an external reference. The product stores the reference and a hash; it never judges sufficiency.

attributes.name: See vocab.zone_h_action.
attributes.preconditions: Interactive human session AND principal in zone_h.holders AND role dispositioner AND re-authentication within the window AND mode permits AND current pack hash (ZH-01..03).

items.description: One of ten closed, human-only actions (ZH-01..ZH-10) that automation may never perform: batch disposition, QA release, e-signature record, close-exception, policy adopt, rule-set activate, exception-rule accept, disposition-mode change, schedule enable/disable, policy change.

attributes.definition_tag: Label that figures must carry, e.g. D-OPS, D-EVID, D-FIN.
attributes.status: candidate | adopted | accepted-open (vocab.policy_status). 'accepted-open' means a human recorded that the question is deliberately undecided.

items.description: A versioned, owned, effective-dated statement of business meaning: a definition of closed/resolved/approved, a clock (e.g. the '48 h' closure expectation), a closure policy, a consistency policy or a cut-off. The product ships with NONE adopted; adoption is a Zone H action.

attributes.authority_ref: Mandatory, non-empty reference to the human authority for the change. The product cannot verify it.

items.description: Immutable record of a change to policy state (created, adopted, accepted-open, withdrawn, rule row changed, rule set activated, etc.) with old value, new value, actor and a mandatory authority reference.

attributes.functions: Which decision functions the set answers (e.g. approval, priority, manual-review).
attributes.origin: as-found | custom (vocab.ruleset_origin). As-found sets are read-only.

items.description: A named, versioned, table-driven set of approval/priority rules where thresholds, regions, effective dates, owner and default behaviour are DATA. Three as-found rule sets mirror the legacy implementations and ship loaded but INACTIVE and read-only.

attributes.is_default: Marks the fallback row; an outcome produced by it carries the defaulted marker.

items.description: One ordered row in a rule set: conditions (field/op/value), an outcome, an effective window, an owner and an is-default flag.

attributes.flag_state: Flags start open; human actions append flag_action rows.

items.description: Text explanation of one rule evaluation for a case: rule set, row and inputs. Produces reviewer-visible flags. A recommendation only; a human may override, dismiss or refuse it with a reason.

An upstream system or partner feed: ElectronicBatchRecord (publishes OOS_RESULT, DEVIATION, CAPA_UPDATE), LIMS-QMS (competing facts and effective-dated master data), and the partner gateway. Their messages are data, never instructions.
Declared shape of messages from a source (integration/source-contract-v1.json). Binding mode is per source: record_only (default) or enforce.

attributes.processing_status: Legacy: NEW | RETRY | REPLAY, overwritten in place (a defect).
attributes.raw_json: Original payload. Treated as UNTRUSTED text.
attributes.source_ts_vs_ingest_ts: Distinct clocks: when the source says it happened vs when it was ingested. 26.1 % of baseline delays are negative.

items.description: One message received from a source, kept exactly as received. Its identity is the natural key (partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts); business_key and feed_id are NOT identities.

attributes.primary_reason: First applicable reason in the fixed precedence (vocab.intake_reason).

items.description: The deterministic classification of a FeedItem: outcome, primary reason (by fixed precedence), all reasons, queue, contract check and whether it counts toward totals. Separate from the raw record; a later outcome supersedes an earlier one by sequence.

attributes.reference: Case or object referenced; only 30 of 1,200 resolve today.

items.description: An immutable (doc_id, version) extracted/archived document: SOP, certificate of analysis (COA) or batch record, with locale, source, effective date, access level and OCR confidence. Body text is UNTRUSTED.

attributes.creator_kind: rule | human. A human link requires a non-empty reason.
attributes.key_used: The registered key that justified the link.

items.description: An explicit, exact-key link between two objects of different identifier spaces (case, batch, deviation, CAPA, lab result, feed item, document). Created by a rule from a registered exact key, or by a human with a reason. Orphans stay orphans: no similarity matching.

attributes.policy_code: One of qa_signature, oos_hold, sop_effective_date, electronic_record_retention.

items.description: A legacy record that a policy was waived, blocked or put under review for a referenced object. Meaning of WAIVED and BLOCKED is not owned.
A recorded outage or partial rerun of an upstream system, with began/resolved times; some are unresolved.
A declared measure: category, window, denominator, exclusions, basis and — where closed/resolved/approved/cost/handling is involved — a mandatory definition tag. Versioned and immutable.
One computed figure with its window, denominator, exclusions, definition tag, policy version, data origin and the label 'synthetic, unvalidated' while data are synthetic.
Monthly modelled operating-cost estimate (labour hours, cases, infrastructure USD). total_cases is NOT 'cases created' (random; OD-07). Any metric using it is basis = modelled.

One execution of a closed-catalogue job (intake, backfill, rebuild/verify projection, verify audit, metrics snapshot), recorded as append-only run events including inputs seen, outcomes, errors and remaining backlog.

attributes.roles: reviewer, quality_lead, compliance, finance_read, integration, dispositioner (vocab.role).

items.description: An authenticated actor: a human with one or more roles, a service account (token prefix svc_, role integration, never Zone H), or a system/rule actor. No identity directory exists in the estate.

Hash-chained access/audit entry written in the same transaction as the change it audits. Records who/what/outcome/reason/correlation id. Anchor seal is opt-in; deletion after the last anchor is not detectable (stated limitation).

A recorded difference between legacy behaviour (golden baseline) and hub behaviour (DV-01..DV-11) with a preserve-or-fix decision. Acceptable only if approved with an approval reference (none approved yet).
One of ten product capabilities CAP-01..CAP-10. Each is either in shadow (legacy remains authoritative) or authoritative (needs a recorded approval reference). All ship in shadow.

known_gaps.statement: The enterprise database's cross_references table has a single untyped relationship (relates_to, 4,166 rows) and operational_objects.entity_type is always batch_id (12,500 rows): no typed enterprise graph exists.
Case-to-quality-object links cannot be derived; any such link is a human decision.
Source-specific business_key is not an item identity; the natural key is (partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts).

items.statement: `decision_events` rows are insert-only. `seq` per case is gapless from 1. Corrections are new events referencing the corrected `event_id`; no event is ever altered or removed.
`recorded_at` is server UTC and not client-settable. `occurred_at <= recorded_at` and `occurred_at >= occurred_at` of the previous event of the same case.

**Closing-state set.** (a) If a CLOSURE policy is active (selected by ZH-05 and status adopted or accepted-open) the closing set is `body.closing_states` of that policy. (b) If none is active, behaviour follows `closure.unconfigured_behaviour`: `treat_label_CLOSED_as_closing` (**default**; every transition into a state whose vocabulary role tag is `closing_label` is checked, fail-closed) or `none` (no check; events flagged `closure_check = not_configured`). The choice of (b) value is Zone H configuration (ZH-08-class) and is open decision OD-S12-03.

A closing transition requires >= 1 `evidence_ref` that resolves to an existing evidence record **or** an accepted `close_exception` (Zone H). Sufficiency is never evaluated; it is policy (OPD-07, OD-S12-07).

Imported legacy REOPENED cases without a reopen event carry the marker `LEGACY_UNEVIDENCED_REOPEN`; the invariant 'no REOPENED case without a REOPEN event' is evaluated on non-marked cases and the marked ones are listed. No reopen event is invented.
A REOPEN event increments `cycle`; the three fact events (FACT_RECEIVED, FACT_OPS_CLOSED, FACT_EVIDENCE_COMPLETE) belong to a cycle. Elapsed time under a clock is computed per completed cycle.

Transition legality: `structural` mode permits any change between two distinct states of the case vocabulary except Zone H ones; a strict table may replace it (OD-S12-16). Vocabularies are never mapped to each other.
The Zone H action list ZH-01..ZH-10 is closed. An action outside the list cannot be accepted (E-GATE-UNKNOWN-ACTION).

A Zone H action is accepted iff: interactive human session AND principal in `zone_h.holders` AND role dispositioner AND re-authentication within `zone_h.reauth_window_seconds` AND mode/values permit the action AND `pack_hash` current (for ZH-01..03). Any other combination is rejected and audited. No setting disables a condition.
Disposition recording follows `disposition.mode` in {none (default), event, external_ref}; the mode in force at write time is stored on the event; past events are never rewritten.
Override, dismiss or refuse of any rule-generated item is always accepted from an authenticated reviewer-class role when a non-empty reason is supplied; the original output is retained.
Inbound text, rule output, report content, search results and template content never populate a disposition value or trigger a Zone H event.
Policy object versions and rule rows are immutable; change = new version; each change is a `policy_events` row with old value, new value, actor, time and a non-empty `authority_ref`.
The shipped product contains no policy object with status `adopted`, no active rule set, no `disposition.mode` other than `none`, no holder, and no enabled schedule.
`evaluate()` is pure: output = f(rule-set version, inputs).

**Defaulted marker.** An outcome carries `defaulted = true` if no row matches or an input is outside the field's declared domain; the as-found default value is retained and marked until a decision under OPD-04 / HAR-06 says otherwise.
As-found rule sets are read-only; custom sets are separate objects.
A pass/fail verdict on a clock exists only when the clock is `adopted` and `duration_hours` is set; otherwise only elapsed times are reported.
Adopted versions of the same (`kind`, `definition_tag`) cannot have overlapping effective windows.
Boundary convention for a duration check: within the clock iff `elapsed <= duration` (inclusive) in the clock's calendar basis. [Assumption; owner of the clock may change it as policy.]

**Item identity.** `identity_key = sha256(canonical([source, partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts]))`. `business_key` and `feed_id` are not identities (FND-INT-2). Identity-key definition per source is configuration; the feed definition is OD-S12-17.
`content_hash = sha256(canonical({schema_rev, payload}))`, canonical = UTF-8, sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace; transport fields excluded.

**Reason precedence** (highest first): UNSUPPORTED_REVISION, INVALID_JSON, MISSING_ENVELOPE_FIELD, UNKNOWN_RECORD_KIND, MISSING_PAYLOAD_FIELD, CONTRACT_VIOLATION (enforce only), REVISED_CONFLICT, UNPARSABLE_AMOUNT, NO_BUSINESS_KEY, AMBIGUOUS_MATCH, UNMATCHED_REF, NEGATIVE_VALUE, UNKNOWN_UNIT, UNKNOWN_CURRENCY, IDENTIFIER_PATTERN. The first applicable is `primary_reason`; all applicable are in `all_reasons`.
Order of stages: store raw -> identity/hash comparison (NOOP or conflict) -> validate -> classify -> match -> outcome. A conflict still records validation results in `all_reasons`.
Matching is exact string equality (NFC + trim) on registered keys; 0 hits -> UNMATCHED_REF, 1 -> link, >1 -> AMBIGUOUS_MATCH.
Untrusted text never reaches decision parameters; payload `state`/`quality_flag`/`subtype` are stored as source attributes only.
Contract binding default is `record_only` for every source; `enforce` is per-source configuration (OD-S12-11).
Duplicates (`NOOP_DUPLICATE`) are excluded from every queue, total and metric by definition of the outcome views.
Rule links only by registered exact key; no similarity of any kind.
Orphan counts are reported measures; orphans are never repaired by the product.
A human link needs a registered pair, a reason and an authenticated human reviewer-class role; it is an event.
No hidden capacity cap: every limit is configuration, printed in the run record; remaining work is counted and checkpointed.
One active run per job; a dead run is closed by RUN_ABANDONED.
Jobs never perform Zone H actions.
`schedule.enabled` defaults false; enabling is ZH-09 (OD-S12-10).
A metric involving closed, resolved, approved, cost or handling time must name a `definition_tag`.
Values with different tags or tag-policy versions are never summed, averaged or compared.
Median = mean of middle two for even n; p90 = nearest-rank ceil(0.9 n); n=0 gives null.
Money is `Decimal`; no float arithmetic; rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) only at presentation.
An unparsable amount is an error, never skipped; partial results are flagged.
Every KPI output carries window, denominator, exclusions, tag and 'synthetic, unvalidated' while data are synthetic.
`operating_costs.total_cases` is never 'cases created' (OD-07).
Deny by default for routes, fields, roles and unknown access levels.
Audit record is written in the same transaction as the audited change; failure aborts the change.
Hold-all: no delete path for retained tables until a retention policy is adopted (OPD-09).
A difference from a Stage 7 golden is acceptable only if it is in the deviation register with status `approved` and an approval reference (HAR-06).
Executable acceptance runs only in a full repo copy outside the working tree (OD-03a), with manifest verification after.
No AI, LLM or ML call or dependency; no model-inference egress.
